text: Git branching is an important part of modern version control workflows. When developers work on new features, they create feature branches so their changes stay separate from the main code. This keeps the project stable while work is in progress. Once a feature is finished, it can be merged back into the main branch. Before merging, teams often open pull requests, which allow others to review the code, discuss changes, and suggest improvements. This workflow helps teams catch mistakes early and collaborate more effectively. By using branches, merges, and pull requests together, developers can manage complex projects safely and keep their code organized.
